turkey.title: 25 lb Herb-Butter Convection Roasted Turkey
ingredients: 1 whole turkey (24–26 lb), completely thawed, giblets and neck reserved for gravy
1 lb (4 sticks) unsalted butter, softened to room temperature
5 tbsp Diamond Crystal kosher salt (or 2½ tbsp Morton kosher salt) for dry brine/seasoning
2 tbsp freshly cracked black pepper
1 cup finely chopped fresh herbs (sage, rosemary, thyme, flat-leaf parsley)
Zest of 2 lemons + 2 halved lemons, 2 quartered yellow onions, 1 halved garlic head (for cavity)
3 tbsp neutral high-heat oil (avocado or canola) for brushing outer skin
3 cups low-sodium chicken or turkey stock + 1 cup dry white wine (for roasting pan base)
equipment: KitchenAid Built-In Temperature Probe (plugged into upper-left oven jack)
Heavy-gauge Stainless Roasting Pan + Sturdy V-Rack (rated for 25+ lb)
Double Heavy-Duty Trivets & Insulated Oven Mitts (for 35–40 lb hot pan)
Moat Carving Board + Sharp Carving Knife + Carving Fork
Heavy-Duty Aluminum Foil (18-inch wide for breast tent)
Paper Towels + Silicone Basting Brush + Turkey Lifters
steps: Remove turkey from fridge 45 minutes before roasting; pull giblets/neck for gravy stock and pat skin inside and out bone-dry with paper towels.
Mash softened butter with chopped herbs, lemon zest, 1 tbsp kosher salt, and black pepper; gently loosen breast skin with fingers and spread half the herb butter directly over the breast meat.

Season cavity and exterior generously with remaining salt and pepper, stuff cavity loosely with halved lemons, quartered onions, and garlic, tuck wing tips under, and brush skin lightly with neutral oil.

Set turkey breast-side up on the V-rack in the heavy roasting pan, pour 2 cups stock into the pan bottom, and insert the KitchenAid temperature probe into the thickest part of the breast avoiding bone.
Roast on KitchenAid Convect Roast at 325°F (~3h 30m); around the 2-hour mark, tent the breast loosely with heavy-duty foil once skin turns mahogany-gold and add remaining stock/wine if pan dries.

Pull immediately when breast probe hits 158°F (thighs ~170–175°F); transfer bird to moat carving board, tent loosely with foil for 55 minutes (carryover reaches 165°F) while freeing the oven for Mac & Cheese.
Reserve all pan drippings for gravy, then carve breasts off the bone, slice ½-inch thick across the grain, arrange on a pre-warmed platter, and spoon warm pan jus over the slices.
turkey.make_ahead_tip: Dry-brine the turkey uncovered on a rimmed sheet pan in the fridge 24–48 hours ahead for ultra-crisp skin, and mix the herb butter up to 3 days ahead.

pan_gravy.title: Two-Stage Pan-Dripping Turkey Gravy
ingredients: Reserved turkey neck, heart, and gizzard (skip liver to avoid bitterness)
2 tbsp neutral oil + 6 tbsp unsalted butter (plus reserved turkey pan fat)
1 large yellow onion, 2 carrots, 2 celery stalks, coarsely chopped
8 cups rich low-sodium turkey or chicken stock
1 cup dry white wine (Sauvignon Blanc or Pinot Grigio) for deglazing
¾ cup all-purpose flour (for golden roux)
4 sprigs fresh thyme, 4 sage leaves, 2 bay leaves, 1 tsp whole black peppercorns
2 tsp soy sauce or Worcestershire sauce + 1 tsp apple cider vinegar + kosher salt to taste
equipment: Flat Wooden Spoon (for scraping roasting pan fond)
steps: Stage 1 (Day Before): Brown chopped turkey neck and giblets in oil over medium-high heat until deeply caramelized, then add onion, carrot, and celery and cook 6 minutes.
Pour in stock, herbs, and peppercorns; simmer uncovered 30 minutes to concentrate flavor, then strain through a fine-mesh sieve and chill overnight.
Stage 2 (Right After Turkey Pull): Pour turkey roasting pan drippings through a strainer into a fat separator; reserve ½ cup clear turkey fat (top up with butter if needed) and all dark pan juices.
Place roasting pan across two stovetop burners over medium heat, add white wine, and scrape up every caramelized bit of fond with a wooden spoon; pour this liquid into the separated juices.
In a 4-qt saucepan over medium heat, whisk ½ cup turkey fat/butter with ¾ cup flour for 3–4 minutes until nutty and golden-blond.
Slowly whisk in warm giblet stock and deglazed pan juices until smooth; simmer 8–10 minutes until glossy and coating the back of a spoon, then finish with soy sauce, cider vinegar, salt, and pepper.
pan_gravy.make_ahead_tip: Simmer and strain the entire giblet stock base on Wednesday (it tastes even richer overnight) so Thanksgiving Day is just a 15-minute deglaze-and-whisk sprint while the turkey rests.

dressing.title: Dutch-Oven Stovetop Herb Bread Dressing
ingredients: 2 lb sturdy country sourdough or brioche-challah blend, cut into ¾-inch cubes
1½ sticks (12 tbsp) unsalted butter
2 large yellow onions, finely diced
6 stalks celery (with tender leaves), finely diced
5 cloves garlic, minced
½ cup finely chopped fresh flat-leaf parsley + 3 tbsp minced fresh sage + 2 tbsp fresh thyme leaves
4½ to 5½ cups warm rich turkey or chicken stock (added gradually)
2 tsp kosher salt, 1 tsp cracked black pepper, pinch of grated nutmeg
equipment: Large 7-qt Enameled Dutch Oven with Tight-Fitting Lid
2 Rimmed Half-Sheet Pans (for oven-drying or air-drying bread cubes)
steps: Cube bread into ¾-inch pieces and dry on two sheet pans at 300°F for 20 minutes tossing halfway (or leave uncovered on the counter overnight for zero oven time).
Melt butter in the 7-qt Dutch oven over medium heat; sweat diced onions and celery with 1 tsp salt for 12–14 minutes until translucent and deeply fragrant without browning.
Stir in minced garlic, sage, thyme, black pepper, and nutmeg; cook 2 minutes until aromatic.
Add half the dried bread cubes and 2½ cups warm stock, folding gently; add remaining bread cubes, parsley, and additional warm stock ½ cup at a time until cubes are moist and custardy, not soupy.
Cover tightly, drop heat to lowest simmer, and steam 12–15 minutes so flavors meld and bottom edges lightly toast; fluff gently with a fork, adjust seasoning, and serve hot.
dressing.make_ahead_tip: Dry the bread cubes and dice all onions, celery, and herbs on Wednesday; store dried bread in zip-top bags at room temp and aromatics in the fridge.

sweet_potato_pie.title: Velvety Roasted Sweet Potato Pie
ingredients: 1 unbaked 9-inch deep-dish all-butter pie crust, chilled and crimped
2 lb Beauregard or Garnet sweet potatoes (~2 cups smooth roasted purée)
½ cup (1 stick) unsalted butter, browned lightly and cooled slightly
¾ cup packed dark brown sugar + ¼ cup granulated sugar
3 large eggs, room temperature
¾ cup evaporated milk or heavy cream
2 tsp pure vanilla extract + 1 tbsp dark rum or bourbon (optional)
1 tsp ground cinnamon, ½ tsp freshly grated nutmeg, ¼ tsp ground ginger, ½ tsp kosher salt
equipment: 9-inch Deep-Dish Ceramic or Glass Pie Dish
Rimmed Sheet Pan (to catch spills and ease oven transfer)
Food Processor or Electric Hand Mixer
Pie Crust Shield or Foil Strips
steps: Roast pricked sweet potatoes ahead until fork-tender, peel warm, and blend in a food processor with browned butter until completely silk-smooth (strain if fibrous).
Whisk dark brown sugar, granulated sugar, spices, and salt into warm purée, then beat in eggs one at a time followed by evaporated milk, vanilla, and bourbon.
Pour filling into the chilled 9-inch pie crust set on a rimmed sheet pan, tapping gently twice to release trapped air bubbles.
Bake at 350°F (sharing the oven rack cleanly with Pumpkin Pie) for 50–60 minutes, shielding crust edges with foil around minute 35 if browning fast.
Pull when outer 2 inches are puffed and set while the center 2-inch circle still gives a gentle Jell-O jiggle.
Cool untouched on a wire rack for 2 full hours to room temperature, then refrigerate at least 3 hours (or overnight) before slicing cleanly.
sweet_potato_pie.make_ahead_tip: Bake on Wednesday alongside the Pumpkin Pie—custard pies slice vastly cleaner after an overnight chill and completely eliminate Thursday oven traffic.

pumpkin_pie.title: Silky Spiced Pumpkin Pie
ingredients: 1 unbaked 9-inch deep-dish all-butter pie crust, chilled and crimped
1 can (15 oz) 100% pure pumpkin purée
¾ cup packed light brown sugar + ¼ cup pure maple syrup
3 large eggs + 1 extra egg yolk, room temperature
1¼ cups heavy cream (or 1 can 12 oz evaporated milk)
1½ tsp ground cinnamon, 1 tsp ground ginger, ½ tsp grated nutmeg, ¼ tsp ground cloves, ½ tsp kosher salt
1½ tsp pure vanilla extract + ½ tsp finely grated orange zest
equipment: 9-inch Deep-Dish Ceramic or Glass Pie Dish
Pie Crust Shield or Foil Strips
steps: Whisk pumpkin purée, brown sugar, maple syrup, spices, orange zest, and salt in a large bowl until smooth and glossy.
Lightly beat eggs and extra yolk, whisk into the pumpkin mixture, then slowly stir in heavy cream and vanilla without whipping excessive foam.
Pour custard into the chilled 9-inch pie shell set on a rimmed sheet pan and pop any surface bubbles with a toothpick.
Bake at 350°F side-by-side with Sweet Potato Pie for 50–55 minutes until edges are set and puffed while the center 2-inch circle still wobbles slightly.
Do not overbake (overbaking causes cracks)—pull at 175°F center temp if checking with an instant-read probe.
Cool on a wire rack for 2 hours until room temperature, then refrigerate 3+ hours until fully set before serving with chilled whipped cream.
pumpkin_pie.make_ahead_tip: Bake Wednesday right beside Sweet Potato Pie at 350°F; store loosely tented in the fridge overnight and let sit out 20 minutes before dessert service.

bread_pudding.title: Banana Cardamom Custard Bread Pudding
ingredients: 1½ lb challah or brioche loaf, torn into 1-inch chunks and lightly stale
4 large ripe spotted bananas (3 sliced into coins, 1 mashed into custard)
5 large eggs + 2 extra egg yolks
3 cups heavy cream + 1½ cups whole milk
¾ cup packed dark brown sugar + ¼ cup granulated sugar
2 tsp freshly ground green cardamom + 1 tsp cinnamon + ½ tsp kosher salt
1 tbsp pure vanilla extract + 2 tbsp dark rum (optional)
3 tbsp unsalted butter (for greasing dish & dotting top) + 2 tbsp turbinado sugar
steps: Butter a 9×13-inch ceramic baking dish generously and layer half the challah chunks and half the sliced banana coins evenly across the bottom.
Whisk mashed banana, eggs, yolks, heavy cream, whole milk, both sugars, cardamom, cinnamon, vanilla, rum, and salt until velvety smooth.
Top with remaining challah and banana slices, slowly pour custard evenly over every piece, and press down gently with a spatula so all bread saturates.
Cover tightly and soak in the refrigerator overnight (or at least 1 hour); pull onto the counter to temper for 35 minutes before baking so the ceramic dish never cracks.
Dot top with butter, sprinkle turbinado sugar, cover with foil, and bake at 350°F for 25 minutes covered, then uncover and bake 25 minutes more until puffed, golden-crisp on top, and 170°F inside.
Rest 10 minutes on a wire rack so custard settles slightly, then spoon warm into bowls with salted caramel sauce and chilled whipped cream.
bread_pudding.make_ahead_tip: Assemble completely in the 9×13 dish on Wednesday night so the brioche drinks up the cardamom custard overnight; slide into the 350°F oven right as everyone sits down for dinner!

mac_and_cheese.title: Three-Cheese Baked Macaroni & Cheese
ingredients: 2 lb elbow macaroni or cavatappi, cooked 2 minutes shy of al dente
6 tbsp unsalted butter + 6 tbsp all-purpose flour
5 cups warm whole milk + 1 cup heavy cream
1 lb sharp aged cheddar, freshly shredded (never pre-shredded)
12 oz Gruyère or Monterey Jack, freshly shredded
8 oz fontina or smoked Gouda, freshly shredded (reserve 2 cups total cheese for crust)
1 tbsp Dijon mustard, 1 tsp garlic powder, ½ tsp smoked paprika, ¼ tsp cayenne, 2 tsp kosher salt
1 cup panko breadcrumbs tossed with 2 tbsp melted butter (optional crunchy topping)
equipment: 9×13-inch Deep Ceramic Baking Dish (or two 8×8 dishes)
Box Grater or Food Processor Shredding Disc
steps: Boil pasta in generously salted water 2 minutes short of al dente so it finishes in the oven without turning soft; drain and toss with 1 tbsp butter.
Melt 6 tbsp butter in a 4-qt saucepan over medium heat, whisk in flour, and cook 2 minutes until pale blond and bubbling.
Gradually whisk in warm milk and heavy cream; simmer 5–6 minutes until thickened enough to coat a spoon, then whisk in Dijon, garlic powder, paprika, cayenne, and salt.
Remove pan from heat and fold in three-quarters of the freshly shredded cheeses in handfuls until silky and completely melted.
Fold pasta into the warm mornay sauce, pour into a buttered 9×13 ceramic dish, and blanket with the reserved cheese and buttered panko.

Temper 25 minutes on the counter if chilled; immediately slide into the 350°F Main Oven during the turkey's 55-minute rest window—bake 20 minutes covered with foil, then 15 minutes uncovered until bubbling and golden; rest 10 minutes before serving.
mac_and_cheese.make_ahead_tip: Shred all cheeses and assemble the entire casserole on Wednesday (add an extra ½ cup warm milk before covering so pasta stays luxuriously saucy); pull to temper 25 minutes before turkey exits the oven.

mashed_potatoes.title: Ultra-Creamy Yukon Gold Mashed Potatoes
ingredients: 6 lb Yukon Gold potatoes, peeled and cut into uniform 1½-inch chunks
2 sticks (1 cup) unsalted butter, melted warm
2 cups heavy cream (or 1½ cups cream + ½ cup whole milk), warmed
4 oz cream cheese or crème fraîche, room temperature (secret for silky hold)
4 cloves smashed garlic + 2 sprigs thyme (infused into the warm cream)
2 tbsp kosher salt (for boiling water) + 2 tsp kosher salt & 1 tsp white pepper to finish
¼ cup finely snipped fresh chives (for garnish)
equipment: Potato Ricer or Food Mill (prevents gummy gluey starch)
Silicone Spatula + Heatproof Lid (or slow cooker for holding hot)
steps: Place peeled, evenly chunked Yukon Golds into an 8-qt pot, cover by 1 inch with cold water plus 2 tbsp salt, and bring to a gentle boil over medium-high heat.
Simmer 18–22 minutes until a paring knife slips through the largest chunk with zero resistance; meanwhile, warm heavy cream, butter, smashed garlic, and thyme in a small saucepan.
Drain potatoes thoroughly in a colander, return them to the dry hot stockpot over low heat for 60–90 seconds to evaporate excess moisture.
Pass hot potatoes through a potato ricer back into the warm pot (never use a blender or food processor).
Strain warm garlic-infused cream and butter over the potatoes, gently fold in cream cheese, salt, and white pepper until velvety and pillowy.
Hold covered over a gentle double boiler (or slow cooker on Warm) up to 35 minutes; top with a final pat of butter and snipped chives right before table service.
mashed_potatoes.make_ahead_tip: Peel and cut potatoes up to 6 hours ahead and keep fully submerged in cold water in the stockpot so you only have to turn on the burner when your schedule says go.

green_beans.title: Crispy Garlic Blistered Green Beans
ingredients: 3 lb fresh haricots verts or slender green beans, stem-ends trimmed
3 tbsp extra-virgin olive oil
5 cloves garlic, thinly sliced
1½ tsp kosher salt + ¾ tsp freshly cracked black pepper
½ cup toasted sliced almonds (or crispy shallots)
Zest and juice of 1 fresh lemon + pinch of red pepper flakes
2 tbsp cold unsalted butter (optional glossy finish)
equipment: KitchenAid Air Fry Basket + Rimmed Drip Sheet (or 12-inch Cast-Iron Skillet for stovetop)
steps: Wash trimmed green beans and spin or pat bone-dry with clean kitchen towels so they blister crisp instead of steaming.
Toss beans in a large bowl with olive oil, kosher salt, black pepper, and red pepper flakes until evenly coated.
Arrange in an even layer in the KitchenAid Air Fry Basket with a rimmed drip sheet placed on the rack below (work in 2 fast batches if needed for 3 lb).
Air Fry in the KitchenAid Upper Combo at 360°F for 10–12 minutes, shaking once at minute 6 and tossing in sliced garlic for the final 2 minutes so it toasts golden without burning.
Transfer hot blistered beans to a pre-warmed serving platter, toss immediately with lemon zest, lemon juice, cold butter if using, and toasted almonds.
green_beans.make_ahead_tip: Trim, wash, and thoroughly dry all 3 lb of beans on Wednesday; wrap in paper towels inside zip-top bags in the crisper drawer, and pre-toast the almonds.

dinner_rolls.title: Warm Honey-Butter Buttermilk Rolls
ingredients: 24 par-baked or fresh bakery buttermilk dinner rolls (or 2 pans of pull-apart yeast rolls)
4 tbsp unsalted butter, melted
1 tbsp wildflower honey
1 tsp flaky sea salt (Maldon)
1 tbsp finely chopped fresh rosemary or chives (optional)
equipment: 2 Rimmed Baking Pans or 9×13 Foil Pans
Cloth-Lined Bread Basket (to keep rolls warm at table)
steps: Arrange rolls snugly in baking pans so their sides stay pillowy soft while tops turn golden.
Whisk melted butter and honey together in a small ramekin.
Slide into the 350°F oven alongside Mac & Cheese (or in the KitchenAid Upper Convection cavity) for 12–15 minutes until deeply fragrant and golden.
Brush hot roll tops immediately with honey-butter, scatter flaky sea salt and herbs across the glaze.
Transfer to a cloth-lined bread basket and cover loosely with the linen corners so they hit the table steaming.
dinner_rolls.make_ahead_tip: Use high-quality par-baked bakery rolls or bake homemade dough through the first rise on Wednesday; brush with honey-butter straight out of the oven right before carving ends.

cranberry_sauce.title: Spiced Orange-Bourbon Cranberry Sauce
ingredients: 2 bags (24 oz total) fresh whole cranberries, rinsed and picked over
1¾ cups granulated sugar (or 1¼ cups sugar + ½ cup brown sugar)
1 cup fresh-squeezed orange juice + ½ cup water
Zest of 2 navel oranges (wide strips or finely grated)
1 cinnamon stick + 3 whole allspice berries (or ¼ tsp ground allspice)
2 tbsp bourbon or Grand Marnier (optional, stirred in off-heat) + pinch of kosher salt
steps: Combine sugar, orange juice, water, cinnamon stick, allspice, and pinch of salt in a 3-qt saucepan and bring to a simmer over medium heat until sugar dissolves.
Add fresh cranberries and simmer steadily for 10–12 minutes, stirring occasionally, until about two-thirds of the berries burst and natural pectin thickens the syrup.
Remove from heat (it thickens substantially as it cools), discard the cinnamon stick, and stir in fresh orange zest and bourbon if using.
Cool on the counter for 60 minutes until room temperature, then transfer to a serving bowl and refrigerate at least 2 hours so the sauce sets into a ruby-jewel jam.
Give a quick stir and bring out 15 minutes before dinner service so aromatics bloom.
cranberry_sauce.make_ahead_tip: Make up to 4 days ahead—cranberry sauce improves in flavor as the spices steep and takes zero stovetop burners on Thanksgiving Day.

brussels_sprouts.title: Air-Fry Maple-Parmesan Brussels Sprouts
ingredients: 2½ lb fresh Brussels sprouts, trimmed and halved lengthwise
3 tbsp olive oil
1½ tsp kosher salt + ¾ tsp cracked black pepper
2 tbsp pure maple syrup + 1 tbsp balsamic glaze or apple cider vinegar
½ cup finely grated Parmigiano-Reggiano
⅓ cup toasted chopped pecans (or crispy pancetta bits)
equipment: KitchenAid Air Fry Basket + Rimmed Drip Sheet
steps: Trim stem ends and slice Brussels sprouts cleanly in half; pat dry and toss thoroughly with olive oil, salt, and black pepper.
Spread evenly in the KitchenAid Air Fry Basket with a rimmed sheet pan beneath to catch any oil drips.
Air Fry at 380°F for 15 minutes total, shaking the basket briskly halfway at minute 7 until outer leaves are deeply charred and crispy while centers are tender.
Transfer piping-hot sprouts to a warm bowl and immediately drizzle with maple syrup and balsamic glaze, tossing quickly so the glaze lacquers the crisp leaves.
Shower with grated Parmigiano-Reggiano and toasted pecans and serve immediately while edges crackle.
brussels_sprouts.make_ahead_tip: Trim and halve sprouts on Wednesday and store dry in a zip-top bag in the fridge; whisk the maple-balsamic glaze ahead in a small jar.

dessert_sauces.title: Chilled Vanilla Whipped Cream & Warm Bourbon Caramel
ingredients: 2 cups cold heavy whipping cream + ¼ cup powdered sugar + 2 tsp pure vanilla bean paste (for whipped cream)
1 cup granulated sugar + ¼ cup water (for caramel base)
6 tbsp unsalted butter, cubed at room temperature
½ cup heavy cream, warmed
2 tbsp bourbon (optional) + 1 tsp flaky sea salt + 1 tsp vanilla extract
equipment: Chilled Metal Mixing Bowl + Stand/Hand Mixer with Whisk Attachment
Heavy-Bottomed 2-qt Light-Colored Saucepan (to judge amber caramel color accurately)
Long-Handled Heatproof Whisk + Small Pouring Pitcher
steps: Whip ice-cold heavy cream, powdered sugar, and vanilla bean paste in a chilled bowl on medium-high until billowy medium-stiff peaks form; cover and refrigerate immediately.
For caramel, combine sugar and water in a heavy light-colored saucepan over medium heat without stirring (swirl gently) until syrup turns a deep copper-amber (~6–8 minutes).
Remove from heat and carefully whisk in room-temperature butter cubes (mixture will bubble vigorously) until fully emulsified.
Slowly stream in warm heavy cream while whisking smoothly, then stir in bourbon, vanilla, and flaky sea salt.
Pour warm caramel into a small heatproof pitcher to spoon over hot Banana Cardamom Bread Pudding, alongside generous dollops of chilled whipped cream for both pies.
dessert_sauces.make_ahead_tip: Make the salted bourbon caramel up to 5 days ahead and store in a glass jar in the fridge—just warm gently in a saucepan or the Upper Combo microwave for 45 seconds right before dessert!

host_essentials: Double heavy-duty trivets & silicone/kevlar oven mitts (25 lb turkey + pan weighs ~35–40 lb)
Carving board with deep juice moat + sharp 10-inch carving knife & carving fork
KitchenAid built-in temperature probe + backup instant-read digital thermometer (e.g., Thermapen)
Pre-warmed serving platters, bowls, and insulated gravy boat
Heavy-duty 18-inch wide aluminum foil (for turkey breast tent + covering mac & bread pudding)
2 rolls of paper towels (for patting turkey skin bone-dry before roasting & spill cleanup)
Fat separator (4-cup capacity) + fine-mesh strainer for silky lump-free pan gravy
Empty dishwasher & clear a 24-inch counter landing zone before the turkey pull
Extra rimmed half-sheet pans (for catching pie drips and lining under the Air Fry basket)
Gallon zip-top bags, deli containers, and painter's tape + Sharpie for labeling prepped components
